tei:titleStmt.tei:title: קוֹל אָהֳלָה
Qōl Ohalah — reshut No9 from the Old Sefaradi Tiqun for Shabbat Ḥazon, by Haḇiḇ ben Yitsḥaq Toledano

tei:div.tei:head: Qōl Ohalah — reshut No9 from the Old Sefaradi Tiqun for Shabbat Ḥazon, by Haḇiḇ ben Yitsḥaq Toledano

tei:lg.tei:l: Hark, Oholah sobs! Hark, she screams of bitter captivity.
Hark, Oholiva tears her heart in crying of her captivity!
Honored Reuben’s portion but he has none,
Shimon in a pile of stones is done.
They said of Issachar the son
Zebulun’s mouth shut in passivity,
From mountain to hill fleeing in declivity.
Hark, Oholah...
Buried in mud, how Judah is hidden in,
Widowers Levi and Benjamin
And a sun-pillar was set in the sanctum within,
That wich my youthful indiscretions did abet
Until my soul pays back its debt.
Hark, Oholah...
Joseph and Gad, how they are kicked out,
Asher and Naphtali sent out,
How the camps of Dan were knocked out,
Their tents without any motivity,
And the time for their calamity, festivity.
Hark, Oholah...
Bring in the daughter, more than all others sweet,
Gather her, send her gifts as a treat.
Tell her prophecies ture and complete,
Show all the peoples her beauty elite,
For Jacob Yah chose to be Theirs discrete. (Psalms 135:4)

tei:note.tei:p: The northern kingdom of Samaria, according to Ezekiel 23
The southern kingdom of Judah, according to Ezekiel 23
Some sort of idolatrous object, mentioned several times in the Bible, and according to midrash used in worshipping the sun.
The word “discrete” included to fit the rhyme scheme, as well as to emphasize the idea that Jacob’s portion is specific.
